current.text: His 2025-26 season was the best of his career. He set career highs in points and assists, his usage rose to 28, and he finished 17th.
His usage rose under coach David Adelman. Many teammates missed games last season and Murray was the only one who stayed healthy, which also lifted his role.
He is a projected starter for Denver next to Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokic. DeMar DeRozan joins the bench.
Experts expect his 28 usage and 35 minutes to hold. One ranker is more sure of his role than of any other player in his tier.
His 42 to 43% three-point shooting from last season will probably drop. About 40 to 41% is a reasonable expectation.
Experts rank him around 14th in 9-cat. One says he could maybe finish top 12, and another says he could finish above Tyrese Maxey.
He is a safe pick in the middle of round two and fine as early as the start of round two. He is also a fine round-two partner for Jokic.
Experts call his low ESPN rank a bargain, even after a career-best season.
In an expert auction mock on 2026-10-05, he sold for 37 USD.
One expert targeted him but would pay no more than 34 USD.
One analyst thinks Denver could trade him before the deadline to shed salary, because he doubts Denver can build a top-15 defense while paying both Jokic and Murray over 30M USD.
Denver has a good schedule: 43 games through March 28 and only 14 back-to-backs, one of the lowest counts in the league.
Denver is not expected to rest Murray on purpose.
One analyst projects Denver to win 50 games.

durable.text: He is a strong three-point shooter. He has shot close to 40% or better from three in each of the last four years.
His game has become more about playmaking. One analyst compares him to Tony Parker more than to a discount Steph Curry.
He is a high-volume scorer who adds threes, good assists and a good FG% for a guard. His best categories are PTS, AST, 3PM and FT%. No category is a real weakness.

note: He is a round-two-level guard. In our league, expect him to cost about 35 to 40 USD: Yahoo values him at 40 USD (average cost 37.4 USD), he sold for 37 USD in an expert mock, and he went for 27 USD in our league last season. He has no weak category and adds PTS, AST, 3PM and FT% on volume, so he fits any build and pairs well with Jokic. Early in the season, check whether his usage stays near 28 now that Denver's roster is healthy and DeRozan has arrived, and whether his three-point percentage falls toward 40%.
